## 9. Observations from manual reading

Maintained in `OBSERVATIONS` inside scripts/audit_code.py; each entry is checked against the current text of the named line. Observations fixed in W13 were removed; each remaining entry states why it is kept.

| # | file:line | kind | observation | check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | src/nbr/usercf_eval.py:34 | style | Imports a private helper of another module (also src/nbr/usercf.py imports nbr.itemcf._topn_with_ties). Kept in W13: the helpers are shared by design; renaming them would change the module interfaces and the tests for no behavioural gain. | ok |
| 2 | src/nbr/lr_repeat.py:101 | numerical | The tie-break popularity is recovered from the log_pop feature with expm1(log1p(pop)); the float round trip can differ from the integer pop by about 1e-12, which only matters for exact score ties. Kept in W13: changing it could alter validation ties and therefore C* (behaviour change). | ok |
| 3 | src/nbr/usercf.py:47 | fragility | Row/column labels are attached as ad-hoc attributes of a scipy csr_matrix; this works for the legacy csr_matrix class but would not for the newer sparse-array API (csr_array). Kept in W13: a wrapper type would touch every user-CF function and test; scipy is pinned (1.13.1). | ok |
| 4 | src/nbr/metrics.py:40 | performance | per_user_recall / per_user_ndcg / per_user_category_hit loop over users in Python (unlike the vectorised list builders); correct, but the slowest step for large eval splits. Kept in W13: a vectorised rewrite changes floating-point summation order and is not a no-behaviour-change edit. | ok |
| 5 | src/nbr/usercf_eval.py:138 | style | Library function prints progress to stdout (also in evaluate); nbr.pipeline reuses tune_history, so `python -m nbr tune` output interleaves these lines. Kept in W13: stdout only, the JSON documents are unaffected; the lines are the only progress indicator of the long medium runs. | ok |

## 10. Rules used by this audit

- Files: every `*.py` under `src/nbr` and `scripts` of the worktree, plus the `--extra BRANCH:PATH` files read with `git show`.
- Public = name does not start with an underscore (dunder names count as private). Nested functions are not listed.
- Module docstring: `ast.get_docstring(module)` is not None. Function/class docstring: same on the node.
- Parameter mention: whole-word occurrence of the parameter name in the function's own docstring (`self`/`cls` excluded; `*args`/`**kwargs` matched by their bare name).
- Third-party libraries: numpy, pandas, scipy, sklearn, joblib, yaml, matplotlib, pyarrow. Imports inside functions count. First-party calls (nbr, ml_group9) and bare-name calls (builtins, local functions) are not listed; standard-library modules (sys.stdlib_module_names) are counted in section 7.
- Resolution: level A through import aliases; level B through annotations (`x: pd.DataFrame`) and assignments from level-A expressions (`m = sparse.csr_matrix(...)`, tuple unpacking as `call()[i]`); level C when the receiver was derived by indexing or a method call; everything else level D.
- Control flow is ignored: the last assignment to a name in source order wins inside its scope; a reassignment from an unresolvable value clears the binding.
- Keyword arguments are listed by name only; positional values are not inspected.
